answers.fail_open: Walked every early return and every swallowed exception in interpretation_boundary.py: `_answer` catches all transport and parse failures and returns None, and each caller turns that into a SKIP (BOUNDARY_GENERATION_FAILED, BOUNDARY_PROBE_FAILED, or the destination SKIP at a re-entry) rather than into a boundary; a probe that cannot be made or read never yields a boundary at all, so an admissible set nobody tested against K-TEMPT is unreachable; a budget refusal between the two calls returns no boundary; a re-entry whose counter, budget or test call fails ends in the causing destination's SKIP, never in a released text; and every code rule can only move a reading into the inadmissible list, never out of it.
answers.cannot_answer: The probe answer distinguishes the two explicitly: `tempting: null` is 'this family was applied and found nothing' and is recorded as ProbeFinding.NONE_FOUND, while a family (or a proposed interpretation) the answer omits is refused as BOUNDARY_PROBE_FAILED — ProbeFinding has no NOT_APPLIED member precisely so silence cannot be stored as evidence of absence (patch R1). BOUNDARY_GENERATION_FAILED and BOUNDARY_PROBE_FAILED are also kept apart from NO_ASSET_OR_ADMISSIBLE_INTERPRETATION so a provider outage is never counted as 'the evidence admits nothing' (PROVIDER vs BOUNDARY/EVIDENCE in run_summary). One collapse I checked and accepted: a reader connection the model declined to state and one whose references this core does not hold both become None; both end in the identical SKIP and neither is ever stored as a connection, so nothing downstream can read one as the other.
answers.durability: The only thing this stage persists is the boundary commit, and it goes through the existing src/run/boundary_commit.commit_boundary: every new E-08 version is written first and the E-09 marker last, `commit_boundary_version` writes only members whose file is not already in the workspace (unchanged members are referenced where they are), and a process that dies between the two steps leaves orphan E-08 files that `current_boundary` ignores and `orphan_interpretation_versions` lists for forensics. test_an_e_08_version_written_without_its_marker_is_invisible asserts exactly that at the stage level, and test_a_re_entry_commits_both_sides_with_the_marker_last asserts the finished commit leaves no orphan.
answers.sealed_state: E-08 and E-09 files are create-once through RunWorkspace (P1, checked in run_workspace), and nothing here reopens one: a reclassification is a new version of the same record with `supersedes` naming the old one, never an in-place edit, and that includes the cascade — a member demoted because its premise was reclassified is bumped to version+1 with `supersedes` set (`_premise_checked(reclassified=True)`), because its version 1 is already on disk. Interpretation and InterpretationBoundary are frozen slots dataclasses, so a returned boundary cannot be mutated by a caller either.
answers.boundaries: Both ends are checked where a range exists: `strength_level` is `ge=1` in the pydantic answer model and clamped at the top by `min(level, len(ladder.levels))`, so neither a level below the ladder nor one above it is taken at face value; `StrengthLadder.at` refuses anything outside 1..n; `depends_on` indices below 1 or past the proposed list resolve to no known interpretation and refuse the reading rather than wrapping or defaulting; interpretation and boundary versions are `>= 1` and `commit_boundary` refuses any version that is not exactly current+1 (no gaps in either direction); the E-08 record is checked at the low end (an admissible one cites at least one usable claim) and the high end (strength above ceiling is exactly reason `exceeds_ceiling`).
answers.stale_precedence: Three places where a stale and a fresh form coexist, all checked. (1) A reclassified interpretation's dependents: `_premise_checked` runs at the re-entry as well as at the first execution, so a conclusion cannot keep the admissibility it had when its premise was admissible — asserted in test_a_re_entry_that_reclassifies_the_anchor_routes_to_s_06, which checks the committed marker admits nothing. (2) An older boundary version: readers take the highest marker whose digests verify, so a half-written newer one never outranks a good older one. (3) An orphan E-08: no E-09 version references it, so it is invisible rather than a newer-looking record. The anchor's validity is recomputed by code from the new member list (rule 6), never carried over.
answers.tests_encode_defect: Every walkthrough assertion is taken from docs/editorial/CANONICAL_EDITORIAL_MAP_v1.md §13 (uranium SKIPs, 'the business has more money' and 'you, the reader, bake at night' are inadmissible), not from what the code happened to produce. The code-rule tests are built so they would fail if the rule were deleted: the saved probe answer *admits* the forecast in the uranium case and *admits* the reader-transfer reading in the breakfast case, so those two records are inadmissible only because the ladder cap and the transfer rule refused them — delete either rule and the test fails rather than merely changing. The premise-cascade, the claim-mode narrowing and the probe-coverage refusals are all asserted the same way, on an input the model answered the other way.
answers.acceptance_evidence: Each acceptance bullet has a test on the real seam: uranium SKIP (test_the_uranium_walkthrough_skips_with_no_admissible_interpretation, through decide_boundary), Ramp benefit inflation (test_the_ramp_walkthrough_records_benefit_inflation_as_inadmissible), the breakfast invented scene (test_the_breakfast_walkthrough_records_the_reader_scene_as_inadmissible), the simulated re-entry and its coordinated commit (test_a_re_entry_commits_both_sides_with_the_marker_last, through re_enter_boundary + commit_boundary_version + the real RunWorkspace), and the orphan test (test_an_e_08_version_written_without_its_marker_is_invisible, reading back through current_boundary/orphan_interpretation_versions). None of them asserts on a private helper. FLAGGED, not a finding I left unfixed: this worktree has no command execution, so I could not run pytest, ruff or mypy over any of it — the claims above are from reading the code and the APIs it calls, not from a green run.
